summary: Quarterly health check focused on a recent usage spike and upcoming model rollforward. Team triaged unexpected token usage variance tied to a new chat flow and clarified tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated deployment for the planned canary. Agreed on three technical follow-ups (benchmark, cost scenarios, compliance docs) and a tentative rollforward week.
topics: latency SLOs and tail p99 behavior
canary rollout timeline and rollback plan
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-26 16:00 PT | Duration: ~58m | Recording: internal | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ben (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM), Liam (Head of ML), Priya (Platform Eng), Darryl (VP Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, quick agenda — usage spike triage, cost impact, and then rollout timing. Does that sound right?
[00:08] Darryl: Yeah that's good, we really want to understand the delta from last quarter, costs spiked and product is nervous.
[00:14] Liam: Quick context — we pushed the new multi-turn assist on March 10th and token counts jumped, also more long form summaries.
[00:22] Priya: And we saw p99 latencies creep during peak at around 2pm UTC, which caused a couple of timeouts in the frontend.
[00:30] Ben: Right, so initial hypothesis — longer average context + lack of prefix caching, plus batch sizing hitting a bad tail. We need to distinguish model compute vs infra queuing.
[00:44] Liam: We did increase max_context to 12k for the flow but actual tokens average was 1.6k and 99th was about 7.8k, so that explains the cost jump.
[00:55] Maya: OK, so two levers: reduce effective context using prefix trimming or enable KV cache and consider lower quantization on the dedicated side.
[01:05] Darryl: Can you remind us of the delta between hosted and dedicated costs at those lengths? We heard rough numbers but not apples to apples.
[01:12] Ben: Sure — ballpark: hosted with the curated large model charges per effective output tokens; dedicated amortizes GPU but has base reservation and autoscale. For long context the per-token CPU/GPU ratio matters. We'll run a proper comparison with the same sequence lengths.
[01:25] Priya: We also have regulatory constraints for EU traffic — data residency, must be in EU region and KMS integration.
[01:33] Sofia: We can do region pinning and KMS; I'll share the VPC checklist and key rotation docs.
[01:39] [02:00] Maya: Let's drill into the spike root cause, Liam — you mentioned an unbounded prompt template?
[02:08] Liam: Yeah, we added a ‘full-history’ toggle for context retention for advanced users and some sessions flip it on, which keeps appending user turns.
[02:16] Priya: There's also a bug where the UI didn't truncate system messages — so a few sessions had huge system prompts.
[02:24] Darryl: Oof, ok. So product will patch the UI; that reduces variance but we still need infra options.
[02:30] Ben: From the infra side, assuming average >4k tokens, we should recommend enabling KV cache for repeated contexts and switching to int8 quant on dedicated for cost savings — that'll reduce memory and token compute by roughly 20-35% depending on model.
[02:48] Liam: When you say int8 quant, are we likely to see quality regressions?
[02:53] Ben: Small delta on some instruction-sensitive prompts; we should validate on your eval set. We'll flag any regression with your prompt cases.
[03:02] Maya: Noted — Ben will run quantized vs float benchmarks with your flagged prompts.
[03:10] [06:00] Priya: We also saw a burst pattern coming from a specific client integration, about 8% of total calls but 25% of 99th tail. Would throttling or rate limits help?
[06:12] Maya: Rate-limiting can be a short-term guardrail — we can suggest per-route quotas in the console. But the longer-term fix is prompt trimming + KV cache + batching.
[06:25] Darryl: For the canary rollforward, we need an SLA plan: if p99 > 2.5s or errors >0.5% we automatically rollback. Is that feasible?
[06:35] Ben: Yes, we can configure canary with health thresholds. We'll instrument tracing to break down tokenization vs kernel time.
[06:43] Maya: Timeline — product aims to ship patch for prompt trimming next week, target canary week of Apr 6. Does that work for you?
[06:52] Liam: Yes but we need benchmarks first.
[07:00] Ben: I'll run two bench sets: hosted with your traffic replay and dedicated reserved pool (2xA10 equivalent) with int8 and float32. Expect CSVs + graphs.
[07:12] Priya: For hosted tests, we need request signing and a test key; can you set that up?
[07:20] Maya: We'll provision a temporary test key scoped to replay endpoints.
[07:26] [18:00] Darryl: On cost modeling — can you show scenarios for aggressive quant + batching vs conservative? We need to present to finance.
[18:08] Maya: Yes — we'll build sensitivity: three scenarios (no quant, int8, int4-ish experimental) and three batch policies (latency-first, balanced, cost-first). That'll give a matrix of projected unit cost.
[18:20] Liam: I want the per-100k request $s and also an annualized delta if we commit to Dedicated reservations.
[18:27] Ben: Reservation math depends on sustained qps; we can model break-even points.
[18:33] [30:00] Priya: Quick security note — we need audit logs to show model input redaction and token-level retention TTLs. What's Redwood's retention options?
[30:12] Sofia: We have configurable retention windows, can disable retention, and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. KMS for key control is supported; I'll attach the paper.
[30:24] Darryl: Good. Also procurement wants SOC2 and penetration test evidence.
[30:30] Sofia: I'll include the SOC2 attest and recent pentest summary in the packet.
[30:36] [38:00] Ben: For the canary rollback plan — recommended steps: (1) start 2% traffic to new model, monitor p50/p95/p99 and error rate, (2) if p99 increases >15% or error rate >0.5% for 5m, throttle to 0 and revert config, (3) postmortem and patch. We'll provide runbook doc.
[38:25] Liam: That sounds good, but can we get automatic throttling based on token-length spikes?
[38:31] Ben: You can configure request filters by token-length or user tier; console supports route-based rules.
[38:38] [46:00] Darryl: Any third-party vendor risks we should flag? We heard about Anthropic's approach but we run hybrid.
[46:10] Maya: Competitor note: Anthropic has stronger chat tuning for safety in some flows. OpenAI has throughput advantages for short chat. Our differentiation is predictable economics and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private.
[46:32] Priya: Final question — how much effort to do an internal dry-run of the rollforward in your staging?
[46:40] Ben: We can stage the model in a private VPC stack; need your traffic replay and a staging key. It's a 2-3 day turnaround to spin up test pool with reserved GPUs.
[46:52] Maya: So action roundup, Ben will run benchmarks, Sofia will send security docs, Maya sends cost model, Liam shares traffic shape, and Priya will provision replay.
[47:05] Darryl: Great. One more: P99 alerting — who on Redwood will we ping?
[47:12] Sofia: On-call + your CSM (that's me) + AE (Maya) — we'll include escalation matrix.
[47:20] [55:00] Maya: Okay thanks all, we'll reconvene after Ben shares the bench results (aiming for Apr 2) and we'll lock the canary window. Any last items?
[55:10] Liam: No, thanks.
[55:15] Priya: Thanks everybody.
[55:20] Maya: Meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription includes small errors (K V cash, quantize asian -> quantization), speaker overlaps occasional.
